**Summary:**

The best move is **Ne4+**. This move gives check to the Black king while simultaneously attacking the undefended bishop on f6. After the king moves (Kg4 or Kh3 are the only legal moves), White plays Nxf6+, winning the bishop. This is a classic knight fork pattern.

**Coaching Note (for 1500-rated player):**
When your opponent's king is exposed, look for knight moves that give check while attacking a piece on the same move—a fork. Here, the knight from g3 jumps to e4, checking the king on h4 while attacking the bishop on f6. Since the bishop has no defender, the king must move, and your knight captures it for free. Always scan for moves where one piece creates multiple threats.
